question: Did company profits, more than rising costs, drive the food price surge of 2022 and 2023?
answer: When every customer expects prices to rise, firms can raise theirs beyond their costs and blame the war. The European Central Bank found profits contributed more than wages to euro-area price growth in 2022, and grain traders, fertiliser makers and some manufacturers posted record earnings. The margin moved upstream, away from the checkout.
move: Whichever side you took, the answer depends on which link in the chain is measured.
ask: Which link of the chain do I blame for a price, and have I checked the others?
counterpoint: Britain's competition authority examined grocers in 2023 and found their margins had fallen, not risen, as energy, wages and wholesale prices climbed. UK food inflation peaked above 19% in March 2023 and eased as those costs fell back. Retail grocery margins are a few pence in the pound; there was little room to gouge.
reference: Competition and Markets Authority, Competition and cost of living: the UK grocery sector, 2023
